name: Beringia
what: A land as big as British Columbia between Siberia and Alaska, a cold grassland with mammoths, horses and bison.
why: People lived here for thousands of years before moving into the Americas; the Bering Strait flooded about 11,000 years ago.

sources.cite: Jakobsson, M. et al., "Post-glacial flooding of the Bering Land Bridge dated to 11 cal ka BP", Climate of the Past 13, 991-1005 (2017)

name: Doggerland
what: Rolling plains, rivers and marshes joining Britain to the continent, home to Mesolithic hunters and fishers.
why: The rising sea drowned it bit by bit; the Storegga tsunami about 8,150 years ago may have swept its last islands.

sources.cite: Weninger, B. et al., "The catastrophic final flooding of Doggerland by the Storegga Slide tsunami", Documenta Praehistorica 35, 1-24 (2008)

name: Sundaland
what: Sumatra, Java, Borneo and the Malay Peninsula joined in one subcontinent crossed by great rivers.
why: Modern humans walked to Java and Borneo; the deep Wallace line still had to be crossed by boat.

sources.cite: Voris, H. K., "Maps of Pleistocene sea levels in Southeast Asia: shorelines, river systems and time durations", Journal of Biogeography 27, 1153-1167 (2000)

name: Sahul
what: Australia, New Guinea and Tasmania as one continent.
why: Getting here took at least eight sea crossings, the oldest known open-sea voyages.

sources.cite: Voris, H. K., "Maps of Pleistocene sea levels in Southeast Asia: shorelines, river systems and time durations", Journal of Biogeography 27, 1153-1167 (2000)

name: Bassian land bridge
what: Dry land joining Tasmania to the mainland.
why: Flooded as the ice melted; Tasmanians were then isolated until 1642.

sources.cite: Lambeck, K. & Chappell, J., "Sea level change through the last glacial cycle", Science 292, 679-686 (2001)

name: Gulf Oasis
what: The Persian Gulf basin as a well-watered river valley fed by the Tigris, Euphrates and springs.
why: A possible refuge for people in Arabia, drowned between 12,000 and 8,000 years ago.

sources.cite: Rose, J. I., "New light on human prehistory in the Arabo-Persian Gulf Oasis", Current Anthropology 51, 849-883 (2010)

name: India–Sri Lanka
what: A land link between India and Sri Lanka across the Palk Strait.
why: People and animals walked between them.

name: Great Adriatic Plain

why: Hunters followed herds across what is now the sea floor off Venice.

name: Laurentide Ice Sheet
what: Ice up to 3 km thick over most of Canada, reaching south of the Great Lakes.
why: Ice sheets locked up so much water that the sea fell, and they pushed plants, animals and people south.

sources.cite: Batchelor, C. L. et al., "The configuration of Northern Hemisphere ice sheets through the Quaternary", Nature Communications 10, 3713 (2019)
